George Abraham Grierson\.
*Linguistic Survey of India, Volume IX, Part II: Specimens of the Rajasthani and Gujarati*\.
Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing, India, Calcutta, 1908\.
LSI p\.52 identifies Rangri as a form of Malvi spoken by Rajputs of Malwa proper\. Both specimen headers, pp\.249 and254, specify State Dewas, Junior Branch\. Canonical Malw \(Glottolog malv1243\) is retained despite legacy display name Malwai\. Shared grammar attribution follows the explicit p\.54 rule; Malvi\-only and other\-lect controls remain excluded\. Superior DSAL original grayscale pages govern readings where binary scans lose diacritics; original Commons DjVu and alternate PDF remain documented comparison witnesses\.
